item.title: Prisoner Exchanges Agree, Ebola Funds Stalled, Impeachment Derailed: On Air, November 12, 2026
item.description:
Twelve senators who caucus with the Democrats are lobbying congressional leadership to remove defense cooperation provisions from the Fiscal Year 2027 National Defense Authorization Act. Maryland Senator Chris Van Hollen led the letter to leadership objecting to provisions that synchronize cooperative efforts and bilateral defense technology research. Vermont Senator Bernie Sanders announced that he will not support Chuck Schumer to serve as Senate majority leader.
The Israeli military and the Israel Security Agency stated that a strike on a five-storey structure at Nasser Hospital in Khan Yunis targeted Muhammad Abu Ismail, whom the military identified as the commander of Hamas's Khan Yunis Brigade. Surgeon Dr Rizq Abu Shaira and a 13-year-old boy were among the six people killed in the strike. Gaza civil defense personnel recovered the bodies from the damaged structure where intensive care and surgical facilities sustained severe damage.
Russian and Ukrainian negotiators concluded two days of United States-mediated peace talks in Abu Dhabi without reaching a breakthrough on territorial disputes or a ceasefire. United States negotiators Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner led the discussions, which lasted nearly five hours on the first day and under two hours on the second day. The delegations agreed in principle to a large-scale prisoner exchange of prisoners of war, with details to be finalized. Davyd Arakhamia from Ukraine stated that the negotiations possessed good momentum, while Vladimir Medinsky from Russia categorically rejected territorial swaps.
Pakistan released Dr Uzma Khan and Noreen Niazi from Kot Lakhpat Jail in Lahore after the federal government suspended their detention orders under Section 3 of the Punjab Maintenance of Public Order Ordinance. The two sisters had been imprisoned for 53 days following their arrest on September 21 ahead of a planned anti-government protest march by the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf party. A third sister, Aleema Khan, remains incarcerated in prison. PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan played a key role in securing the release.
United States special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner arrived at the Kremlin in Moscow for discussions with Russian President Vladimir Putin following the trilateral peace talks in Abu Dhabi. Kirill Dmitriev, Putin's special envoy, met the United States negotiators at Vnukovo Airport and accompanied them to central Moscow. Vladimir Putin stated during the Kremlin meeting that the presence of foreign troops in Ukraine is unacceptable and that any deployed foreign forces would be considered legitimate targets.
Eleven Democratic members of the House of Representatives missed a key floor vote, enabling House Republicans to derail an impeachment resolution against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. The House voted 211 to 204 to refer the articles of impeachment to the House Judiciary Committee, effectively terminating the measure before the 119th Congress ends on January 3. Outgoing Republican Representative Thomas Massie from Kentucky introduced the resolution, alleging unauthorized military actions involving Iran, Yemen, and strikes in the Caribbean.
Six months into the Democratic Republic of Congo's Ebola outbreak, medical charity Doctors Without Borders warned that international aid is failing to reach patients, frontline workers, and communities. The outbreak surpassed 11,042 confirmed cases with 5,387 deaths, driven by the rare Bundibugyo species that lacks approved treatments or vaccines. Medical workers and hospitals face severe supply shortages and unpaid staff while the virus continues to spread.
Full bias analysis and source spectrum: https://news.voidvision.org/onair/.

item.title: Courts Advance Defamation Case While Strikes Disrupt Madrid: On Air, November 11, 2026
item.description:
U.S. District Judge Jeffrey Kuntz denied a motion from the BBC to dismiss a defamation lawsuit brought by Donald Trump. The legal action centers on a twelve-second broadcast segment from October 28, 2024, which spliced together two separate parts of a speech delivered by Donald Trump on January 6, 2021. The case now proceeds toward trial in Florida federal court.
Russia's ambassador to the United States, Alexander Darchiev, died on November 11 at the age of 66. The Russian Foreign Ministry announced his passing, stating he died suddenly without providing a cause of death. Russian President Vladimir Putin had appointed Darchiev to the Washington post in March 2025.
Spain experienced its first general strike in 14 years on November 11. Organized by labor unions UGT and CCOO alongside tenants associations, the 24-hour stoppage disrupted public transport and closed shops. Protesters marched through Madrid and Barcelona demanding lower housing prices ahead of the snap general election scheduled for November 29. The central bank estimates a current housing deficit of approximately 750,000 homes.
Tehran designated the Argentine Navy and Air Force as terrorist organizations on the basis of a 2019 Iranian retaliatory law. The measure responds directly to Argentina designating Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps as a terrorist group earlier in the year. Argentina previously accused the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps of backing Hezbollah and involvement in the 1992 Israeli Embassy bombing in Buenos Aires.
Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guards Navy stated that two oil tankers struck naval mines and suffered massive explosions after attempting to leave through an unauthorized route in the Strait of Hormuz. U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated in Paris that he urged other nations to step up protection for shipping in the region. Indian shipping minister Sarbananda Sonowal confirmed that crew members, including Indian nationals, were safe following maritime incidents in the Persian Gulf.
Joe Biden stated in an interview with People magazine that he would not have sought a second presidential term in 2024 if he had known he had cancer. Biden received a diagnosis of metastatic prostate cancer months after leaving office in 2025. Protests occurred outside Trinity College Dublin on Tuesday as Joe Biden attended an event where his son Hunter received an award from the College Historical Society.
House Republicans voted 211 to 204 on Tuesday to refer eight articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth to the House Judiciary Committee. Representative Thomas Massie of Kentucky introduced the resolution, accusing Hegseth of unauthorized military operations in Iran, Yemen, Venezuela, and the Caribbean. Eleven House Democrats missed the vote due to traffic congestion in Washington, D.C.
British police are assessing fresh abuse claims against Russell Brand after receiving new allegations during and since the conclusion of his trial. Brand began a ten-year and six-month prison sentence after a Southwark Crown Court jury convicted him of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault. The Metropolitan Police investigation relied primarily on witness accounts covering offenses dating between 2004 and 2009.
President Nayib Bukele released video footage on X showing Salvadoran military helicopters firing rockets at a compound in Haiti. Haitian Prime Minister Alix Didier Fils-Aimé praised the commitment of Salvadoran forces in the fight against gangs following the military strike. The targeted property is associated with Wilson Joseph and the 400 Mawozo gang.
Full bias analysis and source spectrum: https://news.voidvision.org/onair/.

item.title: France Blames Iran for Supermarket Hacks and Regional Sabotage: On Air, November 10, 2026
item.description:
France accused Iran of orchestrating a destructive cyberattack that struck commercial refrigeration units in 700 grocery stores on October 11 and 12. French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot called the operation an act of aggression and summoned the Iranian ambassador to Paris. The Paris prosecutor's office opened a formal judicial investigation into the Shahid Kaveh offensive cyber unit.
United States Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated during a press briefing in Paris on Tuesday that Washington does not need to conduct major combat operations against Iran. Rubio pointed to economic sanctions and a naval blockade as successful measures exerting extraordinary economic pressure. The remarks followed closed door talks in Washington involving President Donald Trump and Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani.
At least 12 people died and around 50 others were injured in multiple crashes involving between 50 and 86 vehicles on the Trakia motorway in southeastern Bulgaria on Tuesday. Health Minister Katya Ivkova stated that 10 or 11 people died at the scene near Yambol and Zimnitsa, while another victim died during transport or in hospital. Prime Minister Rumen Radev declared Wednesday a day of national mourning following the disaster.
The United States military relocated at least 10 aircraft from Royal Air Force Mildenhall in Suffolk, England, following a security threat linked to Iran. The operation marks the second withdrawal of American aircraft from a British base in three months following the removal of bombers from RAF Fairford in September. Security threat levels at RAF Mildenhall and RAF Lakenheath were raised to FPCON Charlie.
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth denounced an impeachment push as a political spectacle during a press conference at the Pentagon on Tuesday. The House of Representatives scheduled a vote on a resolution to impeach Hegseth after outgoing Representative Thomas Massie introduced eight articles of impeachment. Vice President JD Vance and President Donald Trump both defended Hegseth and condemned the effort.
President Donald Trump appointed Stephen Miller as the new White House chief of staff following the departure of Susie Wiles. Senator Thom Tillis of North Carolina called the choice an absurd mistake and linked midterm losses to immigration policy management. Katie Miller ended business roles and sold shares in media and technology firms following the promotion.
Russia and Ukraine held four hours of U.S.-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday, marking their first trilateral negotiations in nine months. U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy both described the initial session in positive terms while emphasizing that work remains. The talks focused on humanitarian measures, prisoner exchanges, and security guarantees.
California voters rejected Proposition 40, a ballot measure that sought to impose a one-time five percent tax on state residents with a net worth exceeding one billion dollars. Decision Desk HQ and the Associated Press projected the defeat after nearly 53 percent of voters opposed the measure. Google co-founder Sergey Brin contributed over one hundred million dollars to the opposition campaign.
China's cumulative trade surplus surpassed one trillion dollars in the first ten months of the year, driven by strong global demand for artificial intelligence infrastructure and high-tech manufacturing goods. Customs data released on Tuesday showed that October exports jumped 35.2 percent year-on-year, while imports increased by 41.6 percent. The monthly trade surplus narrowed to 105.3 billion dollars.
An explosion at the Habas steel plant in Aliaga, Turkey, killed 18 workers and injured approximately a dozen others.
Full bias analysis and source spectrum: https://news.voidvision.org/onair/.
